drafts.name: Sarrah Cherhabil

email.subject: Taking Devin from hundreds to thousands
email.body:
Hi Sarrah,

I read that Marco is planning to scale Devin into the thousands, and that Goldman now writes skills like cloud fast track so agents learn how the firm does things.

My guess is the hard part now is less access and more which work goes to agents next, and who keeps those skills current as use cases multiply. Devin picks up the ticket, follows your skills, runs the tests and opens a PR for your engineers to review. Citi is rolling Devin out to 40,000 developers for code, testing and documentation.

Happy to grab 20 minutes. We could pick one team's backlog and map what the next wave would look like. Does this week or next work?

Best,

drafts.linkedin_note: Hi Sarrah, I've been following how Goldman teaches agents firm-specific skills like cloud fast track. I work with banks running Devin at scale and would love to connect and swap notes.
drafts.linkedin_followup: Thanks for connecting, Sarrah. Something I keep hearing from large engineering orgs scaling agents: the bottleneck moves from access to choosing the work. Migrations, test gaps and vulnerability backlogs tend to go first because results are easy to check in CI. Citi is rolling Devin out to 40,000 developers across code, testing and documentation. If useful, I could walk through how other banks pick that next wave in 20 minutes, no slides. Would next week work?

drafts.name: Matteo Pelati

email.subject: AgentGraph and Devin side by side
email.body:
Hi Matteo,

I read about AgentGraph, the agentic tool you built that performs deep static and semantic analysis of codebases and drives Spec-Driven Development toward an evergreen agentic SDLC.

My guess is that once specs and dependency graphs exist, the bottleneck becomes executing changes across many repos. Devin works in its own environment: it clones the repo, runs your build and tests, then opens a PR so reviewers see exactly what changed. Teams using it typically take test coverage from 50-60% up to 80-90%.

Happy to compare notes on how the two could fit together in 20 minutes. This week or next?

Best,

drafts.linkedin_note: Hi Matteo, AgentGraph's approach of building a full dependency graph to drive spec-driven delivery is a smart one. I work on Devin at Cognition and would love to connect.
drafts.linkedin_followup: Thanks for connecting, Matteo. I'd be curious how you think about execution once AgentGraph produces the specs: whether agents run in your own harness or alongside other tools. Devin runs each task in its own environment, runs your build and tests and opens a PR, so it can sit downstream of a spec-driven flow rather than replace it. That keeps your dependency graph and specs as the source of truth. Glad to swap notes for 20 minutes if that's useful.
